n9d326f02048.s: Nehru's broadcast expressing India's independence from power blocs was made on:
n9d326f02048.x: Nehru's broadcast of 7 September 1946 set out India's stand of keeping away from power blocs, a historical root of its foreign policy.

n15b13cccbb1.s: Which one of the following is a principle of Panchsheel (1954)?
n15b13cccbb1.x: Peaceful co-existence is one of the five Panchsheel principles. Non-alignment is a separate policy of India, not a Panchsheel principle.

n819845432f1.s: Which of the following pairs related to Panchsheel is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Panchsheel set out in – Preamble of the India–Tibet Region of China trade agreement
n819845432f1.x: The Panchsheel agreement was signed on 29 April 1954; 1955 is the year of the Bandung Conference.

n9d2b48cdf32.s: A UN General Assembly resolution recognised Panchsheel as a principle of international law in:
n9d2b48cdf32.x: The UNGA recognised Panchsheel in 1957, after its absorption into the Bandung Ten Principles (1955) and before Belgrade (1961).

neb9ec758c54.s: Which one of the following is a core objective of India's foreign policy?
o: Permanent alignment with a single military bloc
neb9ec758c54.x: India's core objectives include independence, security, peace, disarmament and cooperation across ideological lines, not alignment with any military bloc.

n9eb2c434dd4.s: In the Cabinet Committee on Security, the service chiefs attend as:
o: Members in place of the Defence Minister
n9eb2c434dd4.x: The NSA, Cabinet Secretary and service chiefs attend the CCS as invitees; the Defence Minister is a member.

n41cea49e731.s: In the phases of India's foreign policy, the period 1991–1998 is labelled:
n41cea49e731.x: After the USSR's collapse, 1991–98 was the phase of safeguarding strategic autonomy; energetic engagement is the label for 2014 onwards.

n0debcf9306f.s: Strategic autonomy differs from neutrality because it lets India:
o: Stay away from all international disputes
Avoid taking any position on world issues
Judge each issue on its merits without joining military blocs
n0debcf9306f.x: Strategic autonomy means judging each issue on its merits without joining military blocs, so it is active engagement, not neutrality.

n64a151f1837.s: The India-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987, under which the IPKF was deployed, was signed by J.R. Jayewardene and:
n64a151f1837.x: Rajiv Gandhi signed the 1987 Accord with Jayewardene; Indira Gandhi had been assassinated in 1984.

nb3d82d9378c.s: The Hyde Act, a milestone of the Indo-US civil nuclear deal, was enacted in:
nb3d82d9378c.x: The Hyde Act came in 2006, after the 2005 joint statement; the NSG waiver and the 123 Agreement followed in 2008.

n7fa32598d58.s: The Quad of India, the United States, Japan and Australia, first formed in 2007, was revived in:
n7fa32598d58.x: The Quad was first formed in 2007 and revived in 2017.

n18a27c8c046.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's multi-alignment milestones?
o: India became a full member of the SCO in 2017
Act East was upgraded from Look East in 2014
The Quad comprises India, the US, Japan and Australia
The Neighbourhood First policy dates from 2019
n18a27c8c046.x: Neighbourhood First dates from 2014, not 2019. The other statements are correct.

nbbb380a6933.s: The first Voice of Global South Summit was held in:
nbbb380a6933.x: India hosted the first Voice of Global South Summit in January 2023, championing developing countries on reformed multilateralism, climate finance and DPI.

n0456880e35c.s: Under the Instrument of Accession signed by Maharaja Hari Singh, which subject stayed with the State?
n0456880e35c.x: The Instrument (26 October 1947) ceded only defence, external affairs and communications; land revenue stayed with the State.

n96977f833c5.s: In the 1947 Jammu and Kashmir crisis, which event came immediately after the Instrument of Accession?
o: Airlift of Indian troops to Srinagar
n96977f833c5.x: The sequence was tribal invasion, accession, airlift of Indian troops to Srinagar and then the First Indo-Pak war; the UN ceasefire came in January 1949.

n02d7ee8a3b8.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
n02d7ee8a3b8.x: The first Kashmir war was fought in 1947–48, not 1965.

ne1b7edb94b8.s: India's military response to the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025 was:
ne1b7edb94b8.x: After the Pahalgam attack that killed 26 civilians, India launched Operation Sindoor and held the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.

ndf2e87a1c9b.s: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, the western rivers allocated to Pakistan are:
ndf2e87a1c9b.x: The western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab go to Pakistan, though India keeps limited rights such as run-of-river hydropower.

na5e43d9cae7.s: Under Article IX of the Indus Waters Treaty, 'differences' are referred to the:
na5e43d9cae7.x: Questions go to the Permanent Indus Commission, differences to a Neutral Expert and disputes to a Court of Arbitration.

nd2196a31777.s: India's stand on the Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling on the Indus Waters Treaty is that it has:
nd2196a31777.x: India has rejected, not accepted, the PCA ruling, while keeping the Treaty in abeyance and seeking renegotiation.

neb6987a8020.s: India rejected the 2026 ruling of the PCA Court of Arbitration in the Ratle case on the ground that the court:
o: Was appointed by the United Nations
neb6987a8020.x: The Court held the treaty remains in force and issued interim measures; India rejected it, asserting the court had no jurisdiction.

na484354ca79.s: In the Sir Creek boundary dispute, Pakistan relies on the:
na484354ca79.x: Pakistan cites the 1914 map line, while India relies on the mid-channel thalweg principle.

new.s: Under which Article of the Constitution does the Executive make treaties?
new.x: Article 73 covers the Union's executive power, under which the Executive makes treaties; Article 51 is the DPSP on international peace.

new.s: Which entry of the Union List deals with treaties?
new.x: Entry 14 covers treaties; Entry 10 is foreign affairs and Entry 15 is war and peace.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Union List Entry 15 – War and peace
new.x: International peace and settlement of disputes by arbitration is Article 51 (DPSP); Article 73 is the executive power to make treaties.

new.s: Which determinant of India's foreign policy is reflected in its Himalayan frontiers and Indian Ocean position?
new.x: Himalayan frontiers and the Indian Ocean position are the geographic determinants of India's foreign policy.

new.s: Nehru's idealism and Indira Gandhi's realism illustrate which determinant of India's foreign policy?
new.x: Leadership styles such as Nehru's idealism and Indira's realism are the political and leadership determinant.

new.s: The Panchsheel Agreement of 1954 was concluded between Nehru and:
new.x: Panchsheel was set out in the 29 April 1954 India–China agreement concluded by Nehru and Zhou Enlai.

new.s: How many Afro-Asian countries took part in the Bandung Conference of April 1955?
new.x: The Bandung Conference in Indonesia brought together 29 Afro-Asian countries and adopted the Ten Principles.

new.s: The Non-Aligned Movement was founded at its first summit held at:
new.x: NAM was founded at the 1st Belgrade Summit in 1961 in Yugoslavia; Bandung 1955 was the Afro-Asian Conference.

new.s: India hosted which NAM Summit in New Delhi in 1983?
new.x: The 7th NAM Summit was held in New Delhi in 1983; the 6th was at Havana and the 8th at Harare.

new.s: The 19th, and latest, NAM Summit was held in 2024 at:
new.x: The 19th NAM Summit was held at Kampala in 2024; Baku hosted the 18th (2019).

new.s: Which of the following NAM Summit–venue pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: The 4th Summit was at Algiers (1973). The 2nd was at Cairo, the 5th at Colombo and the 13th at Kuala Lumpur.

new.s: Gamal Abdel Nasser, one of the five founders of NAM, led:
new.x: Nasser was from Egypt; Nkrumah led Ghana, Sukarno Indonesia and Tito Yugoslavia.

new.s: The Indira Doctrine of India's foreign policy regarded:
o: Working with rival powers at the same time
Panchsheel as the basis of ties with China
new.x: The Indira Doctrine treated South Asia as India's zone; non-reciprocal goodwill is the Gujral Doctrine.

new.s: Which of the following doctrine–leader pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The Gujral Doctrine (1996) was formulated by I.K. Gujral, not Vajpayee.

new.s: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, a core principle of India's foreign policy, means:
o: Judging each issue on its merits
new.x: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam means 'the world is one family', reflected in the G20 2023 theme 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's core foreign-policy principles:
1. India opposes colonialism and apartheid.
2. India supported the NPT (1968) as a fair treaty.
3. The G20 2023 theme 'One Earth, One Family, One Future' reflects Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India opposed the NPT as discriminatory.

new.s: The first National Security Adviser of India was:
new.x: Brajesh Mishra was the first NSA; the NSA is the secretary of the National Security Council (1998).

new.s: Parliament's Standing Committee on External Affairs scrutinises the Ministry of:
new.x: The Standing Committee on External Affairs scrutinises the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA).

new.s: The Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA) Act was passed in:
new.x: The ICWA Act came in 2001; the ICWA itself was founded in 1943 under Tej Bahadur Sapru.

new.s: India's nuclear doctrine was adopted by the Cabinet Committee on Security in:
new.x: The CCS adopted the nuclear doctrine on 4 January 2003.

new.s: In India's Nuclear Command Authority, the only body that can authorise the use of nuclear weapons is the:
new.x: Only the Political Council, chaired by the Prime Minister, can authorise nuclear use; the Executive Council is chaired by the NSA.

new.s: The Executive Council of India's Nuclear Command Authority is chaired by the:
new.x: The Executive Council is chaired by the NSA; the Political Council is chaired by the PM.

new.s: Which one of the following is NOT a tenet of India's nuclear doctrine (2003)?
o: First use against a conventional attack
new.x: The doctrine rests on credible minimum deterrence, No First Use and retaliation only, so first use is ruled out.

new.s: In the Korean War, India's Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission for prisoners of war was headed by:
new.x: Gen. K.S. Thimayya headed the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission chaired by India in the Korean War.

new.s: The Pakistan army surrendered in Dhaka, completing Bangladesh's liberation, on:
new.x: Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971; 9 August 1971 is the Indo-Soviet Treaty.

new.s: The Farakka Accord on sharing of Ganga water between India and Bangladesh was signed in:
new.x: The Farakka Accord on Ganga water with Bangladesh dates from 1977.

new.s: Katchatheevu was ceded by India to Sri Lanka in:
new.x: Katchatheevu was ceded to Sri Lanka in 1974, during the phase of regional assertion.

new.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Lahore Declaration
2. Simla Agreement
3. 123 Agreement
4. Farakka Accord
new.x: Simla (1972) came before Farakka (1977), the Lahore Declaration (1999) and the 123 Agreement (2008).

new.s: India's Look East Policy was launched in 1991–92 under Prime Minister:
new.x: Narasimha Rao launched the Look East Policy in 1991–92, bringing India closer to ASEAN.

new.s: Besides Look East, India's post-Cold War outreach under Narasimha Rao is known for building ties with:
new.x: In 1991–98, India under Narasimha Rao turned to ASEAN through Look East and opened ties with Israel.

new.s: India's No First Use policy after Pokhran-II was announced by the government of:
new.x: The Vajpayee government announced No First Use; the formal doctrine followed in 2003.

new.s: After Pokhran-II (1998), the United States imposed sanctions on India under the:
new.x: The US used the Glenn Amendment for sanctions after 1998; the Hyde Act (2006) and 123 Agreement (2008) belong to the later nuclear deal.

new.s: The India–US dialogue after Pokhran-II was held between Jaswant Singh and:
new.x: The Jaswant Singh–Strobe Talbott talks followed the sanctions after Pokhran-II.

new.s: During India's G20 Presidency (2022–23), which body was made a permanent member of the G20?
new.x: The African Union was made a permanent member of the G20 under India's Presidency.

new.s: The 1988 action plan for nuclear disarmament is associated with Prime Minister:
new.x: Rajiv Gandhi presented the 1988 nuclear disarmament action plan, besides the Sri Lanka Accord and SAARC.

new.s: The Tashkent Declaration of 1966 was signed by which Indian Prime Minister?
new.x: Lal Bahadur Shastri signed the Tashkent Declaration in 1966; Indira Gandhi is linked with Simla (1972).

new.s: The Lahore Declaration of February 1999 was signed by Atal Bihari Vajpayee and:
new.x: Lahore (1999) was Vajpayee–Nawaz Sharif; the Agra Summit (2001) was with Musharraf.

new.s: The ceasefire line in Jammu and Kashmir was converted into the Line of Control by the:
new.x: The Simla Agreement (1972) turned the ceasefire line into the LoC; Tashkent did not create the LoC.

new.s: Which of the following operation–country pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: Operation Meghdoot (1984, Siachen) was India's; Gibraltar and Grand Slam were Pakistani operations of 1965.

new.s: The 1965 India–Pakistan war was followed by the:
new.x: The 1965 war ended in the Tashkent Declaration (1966); Simla followed the 1971 war.

new.s: UNSC Resolution 47 (1948) on Kashmir called for:
o: A plebiscite conditional on Pakistan's withdrawal
An immediate plebiscite without any withdrawal
Conversion of the ceasefire line into the LoC
new.x: Resolution 47 called for a plebiscite conditional on Pakistan's withdrawal, which was never held.

new.s: After the Instrument of Accession, Indian troops were airlifted to Srinagar on:
new.x: The accession was signed on 26 October 1947 and troops were airlifted on 27 October.

new.s: Article 370 was abrogated and J&K and Ladakh became Union Territories on:
new.x: Article 370 was abrogated on 5 August 2019; it had become operative on 17 November 1952.

new.s: In response to the abrogation of Article 370, Pakistan suspended bilateral trade and the:
new.x: Pakistan downgraded ties and suspended trade and the Samjhauta Express; the Kartarpur Corridor opened later, in November 2019.

new.s: The Siachen dispute concerns the unmarked line beyond the point:
new.x: The line beyond NJ9842 was left unmarked; India secured the glacier in Operation Meghdoot (1984).

new.s: Sir Creek, the disputed estuary between Gujarat and Sindh, is about how long?
new.x: Sir Creek is a 96-km tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch.

new.s: The India–Pakistan Composite Dialogue was stopped after the:
new.x: The Composite Dialogue (1997, restarted 2004) stopped after 26/11 in 2008.

new.s: India's response to the Uri attack of September 2016 was:
new.x: Uri led to surgical strikes; Pulwama to Balakot, the Parliament attack to Parakram and Pahalgam to Sindoor.

new.s: Operation Parakram, a large troop mobilisation, was India's response to the:
new.x: Operation Parakram followed the 13 December 2001 attack on Parliament.

new.s: On withdrawing MFN status from Pakistan in February 2019, India imposed a customs duty of:
new.x: After Pulwama, India withdrew MFN (granted in 1996) and imposed 200% customs duty.

new.s: On the Indian side, the Kartarpur Corridor starts from Dera Baba Nanak in the district of:
new.x: The visa-free corridor runs from Dera Baba Nanak (Gurdaspur) to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, Kartarpur (Narowal).

new.s: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed at Karachi on:
new.x: Nehru and Ayub Khan signed the Treaty at Karachi on 19 September 1960, brokered by the World Bank.
